message: Hello, we found your note directing us to come here. What happens next?

Hello. In the end, we want to get money from you. We’ve encrypted your files and also downloaded a large number of them to our own servers. We can give you a list of the files we took, along with 1‑3 small samples from that list. We can also decrypt 1‑3 small files that contain non‑critical information to demonstrate that we can recover all of your data. If you’d like, we can do all of that, or we can go straight to the payment request. You see a timer counting down the negotiation period. When it expires, if we don’t receive what we want, we will publish the stolen data publicly and delete the decryption tools, making any recovery of your data completely impossible.

Thank you for this information, I will take it to our bosses. How much data do you have in your possession? We would like the list and will collect encrypted file samples to send to test your decryption tool.

We’ve assessed the situation overall and concluded that you’re not interested in resolving this issue. You’re trying to keep it hidden for as long as possible. So, once you read this message, we’ll publish a blog post announcing the incident, with a countdown timer to the data release.

At this point, we are moving through the internal authorization process required before any payment can be approved.      This step involves multiple parties and cannot be expedited beyond certain requirements. We are prepared to reach an agreement with you once this process is completed.   Maintaining the current timeline is critical for us to proceed. Any early release of the information will disrupt this process and may impact our ability to finalize payment.      We expect to continue working within the agreed timeframe and will provide an update as soon as the current phase is complete.

We don't make promises we can't keep. We've now published a blog post with a timer. If you're genuinely interested in solving the problem, you won't let data be published no matter what. If you were interested in maximum incident concealment and delaying consequences by other means, you didn't succeed. What to do next is up to you. Understanding the full depth of consequences for organizations in your industry from such incidents, posts like this on our blog help other companies that encounter us not try to play games.
